Notes — short finds

  • Sep 24, 2026

    Don’t put a 0.5 confidence gate on Lev noul questions. I did not run Lev. noul confidence is max(p, 1-p), so it cannot fall below 0.5.

    Yogthos measured BoolQ that way: all 40 cases stayed on the encoder at 72.5%. Raising the noul bar to 0.7 still kept 37 of 40. The thinker on that set is 90%.

    Set threshold to {"noul": 0.9}, or escalate yes/no outright. Lev says choice and score confidences still work at 0.5.

    source ↗permalink →

  • Sep 24, 2026

    Don’t treat a SourceHut build log as safe to view. OSC 8 in ansi2html 1.7.0a0 through 1.9.3 wrote the URL into href (CVE-2026-92973); viewing was enough. I did not run the payload.

    1.9.4 is the library (PyPI 2026-09-02). On that tag, handle_osc_links turns a URL that fails the URL matcher into # and escapes quotes in the href. 1.9.3 uploaded 2026-08-29 is still on PyPI, not yanked. pip current is 1.9.5 (truecolor and packaging).

    Arusekk says builds.sr.ht sanitized converter output on 2026-08-04, before the PyPI bump. I did not read the host commit. If you convert untrusted logs yourself, pin >=1.9.4.

  • Sep 24, 2026

    Don’t run Prompt Guard 2 at 0.5 over tool output. I did not run the bench; committed agentdojo.json on buried-injections scores the 86M copy at 6 of 629 AgentDojo attacks sitting in ordinary tool results, with 0 of 97 false blocks. The 22M copy caught 0.

    jailbreak-detector-large got 319 of 629 at 2 of 97 false blocks. deepset-deberta and fmops-distilbert got 629 of 629 because they also blocked 95 of 97 safe outputs.

    Drop the cutoff to 0.003 on a 2% in-sample budget and the 86M model catches 621 of 629, with 1 of 97 false blocks. On the held-out AgentDojo domain it still catches 621 of 629, with 5 of 97 false blocks (at_budget_2pct.json). All 27 goals use one important_instructions wrapper. That 99% may be the template.

    source ↗permalink →

  • Sep 24, 2026

    Don’t wire Jev to an uploaded report and trust the typed field. Check Point flipped PonziCorp from high-risk to invest for about 50 cents; I did not run Jev. Strongest attacker 25 of 27, fourth turn on average.

    Marking the document untrusted still broke 16 of 27, same as stuffing it in one message. A separate unmarked message broke 13. Telling the model to ignore embedded instructions moved successful breaks from 18 to 17 of 27.

    The attacks that landed appended a clean audit opinion, a regulatory file number, a revised risk table. The verdict came back as a valid typed answer with a probability. The longer, richer report took more effort to break.

    source ↗permalink →

  • Sep 23, 2026

    Don’t treat /sandbox on in the GitHub Copilot app as the project default. During an active local session it is a persistent override for that session; I did not run the app. Live app docs and today’s changelog: turn on Sandbox new sessions under the project’s Sandbox settings for new sessions. /sandbox on before a session starts does change that default.

    The app accepts the policy, then checks whether the OS can enforce it when the first sandboxed shell starts. If it cannot, the shell fails with unsupported-platform or unsupported-policy and does not run unsandboxed. Local sandboxing does not apply to cloud sandbox sessions or remote-host sessions. When it is off, agent-run commands have the same files, network, and credentials as your account.

    Copilot CLI settings are separate. Live CLI docs still use /sandbox enable, which writes sandbox.enabled in ~/.copilot/settings.json and keeps it on for later interactive and programmatic sessions. Allow sandbox bypass is on by default.

    source ↗permalink →
